subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should the remaining fix stop scheduled producers from requesting invalid memory paths, or should OpenClaw change the generic read tool so directory targets return listings instead of read failures?
rationale: Current source proves only partial fixes and a directory read failure shape; changing generic read semantics affects every agent tool user, while a producer-specific fix cannot be scoped until the scheduled `CORE.md`/`agent-tasks` source is reproduced.

options.title: Reproduce and fix the producer
options.body: Capture a current gateway/cron run with stability diagnostics and repair the scheduled prompt or payload that asks for invalid paths, preserving current read-tool semantics.

options.title: Adopt directory listings for read
options.body: Treat directory targets as a supported read-tool result, with explicit tests and docs for how it differs from list/ls behavior.

options.title: Close only after disproval
options.body: Close this only if a current live run shows the reported scheduler/RSS pattern no longer occurs and the remaining errors are user-authored cron payloads.

recommendation.title: Reproduce and fix the producer
recommendation.body: Capture a current gateway/cron run with stability diagnostics and repair the scheduled prompt or payload that asks for invalid paths, preserving current read-tool semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing candidate among the identified owners for the cross-cutting tool-contract and gateway stability decision.
